metadata.title: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis of PCR Products Using UltraPure Agarose
metadata.purpose: Separate and visualize PCR DNA fragments by classic agarose gel electrophoresis using UltraPure Agarose and reagents.
metadata.scope: Classic 1% agarose gel electrophoresis protocol from the Thermo Fisher UltraPure Agarose web pages. Covers gel preparation, casting, sample loading, electrophoresis, and visualization of PCR products.
beforeYouBegin: UltraPure Agarose is a standard melting temperature, multi-purpose agarose that is ideal for routine separation analysis. UltraPure Agarose resolves DNA and RNA fragments from 500–23,000 bp, and has no detectable DNase or RNase activity.
Refer to the agarose concentration table (table t1) for the recommended concentration of UltraPure Agarose needed to resolve DNA fragments of the approximate listed range.
Remember to take the thickness of the gel into account, as it affects both well volume and power requirements.
The total gel volume will vary depending on the size of the casting tray.
Use TAE or TBE buffer; use the same buffer for gel casting and running.

Add room temperature buffer (TAE or TBE) into a flask that can hold 2–4 times the volume of your agarose solution. Place a magnetic stir bar into the flask. Slowly sprinkle the required amount of agarose powder into the flask as the solution mixes, to prevent the formation of agarose clumps.

For visualization of DNA in the gel, a fluorescent dye can be added to the agarose solution just prior to pouring, or the gel can be stained after electrophoresis. Use of SYBR Safe DNA gel stain in conjunction with blue light transillumination is recommended for gel extraction procedures for cloning purposes.

steps.action: Weigh out 1 g of agarose gel and add it to a 500 mL flask. Add 100 mL of 1X TBE.
steps.criticalNotes: The total gel volume will vary depending on the size of the casting tray.

steps.action: Gently mix and heat the solution in a microwave until the agarose is completely dissolved.
steps.criticalNotes: CAUTION: wear protective gloves when handling extremely hot agarose solution and heat the solution in several short intervals—do not let the solution boil for long periods as it may boil out of the flask or cause a loss to water vapor. You can weigh the flask before and after heating and add distilled water to make up lost volume.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear protective gloves when handling extremely hot agarose solution.

steps.action: Allow hot agarose to cool in a water bath set at 50–55°C for 10 min. Swirl the flask occasionally to cool evenly.
Prepare the gel casting tray by sealing the ends of the gel chamber with tape. Place the 10-well comb in the gel tray.
steps.criticalNotes: Note: pour the gel on a level surface; otherwise, the gel thickness will not be even, resulting in uneven migration.

steps.action: Add 5 µL of stock ethidium bromide solution to the cooled gel and pour into the gel tray. Remove any bubbles and allow gel to cool for 30 min at room temperature.

parameters.rawText: 5 µL of stock ethidium bromide solution

steps.safetyNotes: Exercise caution when using ethidium bromide, which is a known carcinogen.

steps.action: Remove the comb and tape, place the gel tray in the electrophoresis chamber, and cover with 1X TBE buffer.
steps.criticalNotes: Cover the gel with ~2–3 mm of buffer for best results.

steps.action: Add 0.2 µL volume of loading buffer to samples; e.g., 4 µL of 20 µL sample. Load 100-250 ng of your sample and add E-Gel loading buffer to 20 µL.

parameters.rawText: Add 0.2 µL volume of loading buffer to samples; e.g., 4 µL of 20 µL sample

steps.action: Load the first and last wells with 20 µL of diluted markers/ladders (Use 5 µL of E-Gel marker plus 15 µL of water). Continue loading 20 µL of sample per well.

parameters.rawText: 5 µL of E-Gel marker plus 15 µL of water

steps.action: Electrophorese at 100V for 40 min. Make sure that the current is running in the correct direction.
steps.criticalNotes: Make sure that the current is running in the correct direction.

steps.action: After the run, remove the gel with tray and visualize PCR fragment bands using the E-Gel Imager or other blue light source (Safe Imager 2.0 or E-gel Safe Imager).

controls.name: DNA ladder
controls.description: Load the first and last wells with 20 µL of diluted markers/ladders (Use 5 µL of E-Gel marker plus 15 µL of water). Ladder bands serve as a size reference for sample fragments.

controls.name: Negative control
controls.description: No explicit negative control (e.g., no-template control lane) is described in the source protocol.

expectedOutputs: Visible PCR fragment bands visualized using the E-Gel Imager or other blue light source (Safe Imager 2.0 or E-gel Safe Imager).
DNA fragment sizes can be estimated by comparison to the TrackIt Kb Plus DNA ladder loaded in the first and last wells.

troubleshooting.problem: Agarose boils out of flask or loss of water vapor during heating
troubleshooting.cause: Solution boiled for long periods in the microwave.
troubleshooting.solution: Heat the solution in several short intervals—do not let the solution boil for long periods as it may boil out of the flask or cause a loss to water vapor. You can weigh the flask before and after heating and add distilled water to make up lost volume.

troubleshooting.problem: Uneven gel thickness and uneven migration
troubleshooting.cause: Gel not poured on a level surface.
troubleshooting.solution: Pour the gel on a level surface; otherwise, the gel thickness will not be even, resulting in uneven migration.

troubleshooting.problem: Agarose clumps that do not dissolve
troubleshooting.cause: Agarose powder added too quickly to buffer.
troubleshooting.solution: Slowly sprinkle the required amount of agarose powder into the flask as the solution mixes, to prevent the formation of agarose clumps.

troubleshooting.problem: No dedicated troubleshooting table in source
troubleshooting.cause: The linked Thermo Fisher protocol pages do not include a dedicated troubleshooting section for electrophoresis results.
troubleshooting.solution: Consult the Thermo Fisher support center for nucleic acid gel electrophoresis troubleshooting guidance.

safety: Exercise caution when using ethidium bromide, which is a known carcinogen.

CAUTION: wear protective gloves when handling extremely hot agarose solution and heat the solution in several short intervals—do not let the solution boil for long periods as it may boil out of the flask or cause a loss to water vapor.

For the intercalating dye ethidium bromide, use a final concentration of 0.5 µg/ml. If more sensitive detection is required, use SYBR Green I nucleic acid gel stain (Invitrogen Cat. no. S-7563), or SYBR Safe DNA gel stain (Invitrogen Cat. no. S33102). Use of SYBR Safe DNA gel stain in conjunction with blue light transillumination is recommended for gel extraction procedures for cloning purposes.
Exercise caution—microwaved solution may become superheated and foam over when agitated.
limitations: The linked protocol provides a 1% TBE gel recipe. Users should consult the agarose concentration table (t1) for other fragment-size ranges. The protocol does not include a dedicated troubleshooting section or explicit negative/positive controls beyond the DNA ladder.
